# Candidate fixtures

These committed fixtures describe the candidate durable-nonce and server-key rotation profiles. They do not change current v0.1 loaders or assert SDK/runtime support.

| Output | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `rotation-vectors.json` | Exact signed records, overlapping/tie chains, and 19 negative codec/chain cases |
| `nonce-vectors.json` | 24 durable-admission events with hand-stated state/effect expectations |
| `rotation-state-vectors.json` | 14 signed refresh cases and eight clock/server events |
| `../../tests/candidate/CASES.md` | Generated index of the same source expectations |

## Standing CI gate

The candidate job first runs `gen-fixtures.mjs --check` against committed bytes, before any regeneration. It then regenerates, checks determinism, verifies the on-disk fixtures, runs `node --test spec/tests/candidate/*.test.mjs`, and uploads the outputs. A stale committed fixture cannot be concealed by regeneration. Existing top-level v0.1 fixture gates remain unchanged.

Hand-stated expectations live separately from the semantic models. Cryptographic checks include the RFC 8032 known-answer vector, Node verification, and an independent affine-coordinate verifier. These test-only implementations are not production cryptography.

Client `rotation_*` errors are local errors, not HTTP statuses. Only the candidate server-native error mapping is HTTP status-bearing. The normative candidate prose and future implementation acceptance requirements are in `spec/candidate/`.
